entities.summary:
Adolfo Armando Uriona is an Argentine Roman Catholic bishop, serving the Church in one of Latin America's most historically Catholic nations. Argentina's Catholic Church has played a complex and sometimes controversial role in national life — deeply embedded in Argentine culture, identity, and politics, while also carrying the difficult legacy of its relationship with the military dictatorship (1976–1983) that murdered thousands of Argentines including clergy and religious.

The post-dictatorship Argentine Church has been engaged in a long process of reckoning with that legacy while also navigating the rapid social changes of the late twentieth and early twenty-first centuries — including the legalisation of same-sex marriage in 2010 and abortion in 2020, both of which the Church actively opposed. Bishops like Uriona serve within this highly politicised and historically charged context.

His episcopal ministry reflects the Argentine Church's complex navigation of its prophetic and institutional responsibilities in a country where Catholicism retains deep cultural roots even as formal religious practice declines. The Argentine Church is also the homeland of Pope Francis (Jorge Mario Bergoglio), and the Franciscan priorities of the current pontificate have particular resonance in Argentine Catholicism.
